title: The Siege of Vienna
description: September-October 1529. Suleiman the Magnificent's army arrives before Vienna's medieval walls. The player commands the garrison of German Landsknechts and Spanish arquebusiers under Niklas Graf Salm: countermine the Ottoman sappers, repel assaults on the Carinthian Gate, and hold until autumn rains and supply failure force the Ottoman withdrawal.

anachronisms_found: SALADIN is the only placed enemy unit and stands in for Suleiman the Magnificent — Saladin died in 1193, is Kurdish/Ayyubid, and has no connection to the 1529 Ottoman army; a generic Janissary, Sultan-style Cataphract/Elite unit, or an unnamed 'Enemy Lord' would have avoided this

Garrison armed with CROSSBOWMAN and MAN_AT_ARMS in 1529; the engine offers Hand Cannoneers (for Spanish arquebusiers) and Two-Handed Swordsmen/Pikemen (for Landsknechts), so the melee/crossbow roster is an avoidable century error
No gunpowder on either side, though the 1529 siege was defined by Spanish arquebusiers and Ottoman artillery/mining; Bombard Cannon and Janissary exist in the engine
Niklas Graf Salm is represented only by a generic KING unit — a monarch figure inside a city defended by an Imperial field commander is wrong; Vienna in 1529 had no resident king
3,083 TREE_OAK covering a 144x144 map turns the Danube plain and a walled Renaissance city into deep forest; no river, no faubourgs, no Carinthian Gate feature
Generic AoE2 economic/urban set (MILL, MARKET, MONASTERY, UNIVERSITY, STABLE, 6 HOUSES) with only 12 villagers stands in for a city of ~20,000 with 20,000+ defenders

issues_found: Player 2's only placed unit is the hero SALADIN, a 12th-century Kurdish/Ayyubid sultan, standing in for Suleiman the Magnificent (1529 Ottoman) — wrong culture and off by roughly 350 years, and avoidable since a renamed generic Janissary/Elite unit or Persian/Turkish-flavoured unit could have carried the role

The garrison is MAN_AT_ARMS x8 and CROSSBOWMAN x7 — no Landsknechts (available as the Teutonic unique unit) and no gunpowder infantry (Hand Cannoneer / Conquistador) for the Spanish arquebusiers the brief explicitly names
Player 1's leader is a bare KING object rather than an identified Niklas Graf Salm figure; the dialogue names Salm but the placed roster does not
Both active players are set to RANDOM civilization, so Ottoman and Central-European architecture and unit sets are left to chance rather than assigned (Turks vs Teutons/Spanish were both available)
3,083 oak trees dominate the map, making the setting a forest clearing rather than the Danube plain and suburbs before Vienna's walls; no river, no Ottoman siege camp

The brief's distinctive mechanic — countermining Ottoman sappers under the Carinthian Gate — is entirely absent; the Carinthian Gate exists only in one dialogue line, and there is no mine, breach, or damaged-wall representation
The siege is compressed into a single night ('survive until dawn (10:00)'), misdating a three-week September–October investment and reducing it to four generic wave attacks

An 'eliminate all Player 2 objects' victory path and a 'slay the Ottoman commander' path are encoded, though Suleiman was never killed or defeated in the field — the Ottomans withdrew because of rain, disease and supply failure
'Hard Difficulty' adds only two CREATE_OBJECT actions and 'Easy' kills an object — difficulty is not tied to anything historical such as sapper numbers or Janissary quality

The Ottoman besieger is represented by the hero SALADIN, a 12th-century Ayyubid sultan, standing in for Suleiman the Magnificent (1529) — a ~350-year era error that was avoidable, since a renamed generic unit or a Janissary/Turkish elite would have served

Player 2's roster contains literally nothing but the Saladin hero; the entire Ottoman host exists only as unspecified CREATE_OBJECT spawns, so the janissaries, sipahi cavalry and sapper/artillery train central to the brief are not authored as placed content

Both civilizations are left RANDOM, so Viennese/Central European architecture and the Ottoman opponent's building set and unit access are unassigned — the one setting choice the editor makes trivially available is skipped
The garrison is Man-at-Arms and Crossbowmen: no gunpowder units at all, despite the brief's 'Spanish arquebusiers', and Two-Handed Swordsmen/Champions (the natural Landsknecht stand-in) are absent

Niklas Graf Salm is represented by the KING unit rather than a renamed infantry hero, making the defending commander a non-combatant piece rather than the fighting officer who was mortally wounded on the walls
Map is 3,083 oak trees with forage bushes, sheep and gold/stone mines — a wilderness clearing, not the Danube bank and glacis-cleared suburbs of Vienna
The historically decisive countermining war beneath the Carinthian Gate is only mentioned in the brief and never mechanically or spatially represented
The 'hold until dawn (10:00)' framing recasts a three-week siege broken by autumn rain and supply failure as a single night's defence
The 'VC Eliminate' path lets the player win by wiping the besieging army off the map, which the Vienna garrison never attempted and could not have done
